elena.notes: Ranged light poke that gives Elena strong punishes and confirms; allows for 4-light confirm strings after chained 2LPs, but does not combo naturally into 214LK; Special/DI cancel is delayed until after 2nd active frame; DR cancel is delayed until after 3rd active frame

elena.name: 站立中脚 (5MK)
elena.notes: 2f extra recovery on whiff; useful combo and frame trap tool; short range for a 6-frame medium

elena.name: 站立重脚 (5HK)
elena.notes: Low Crush 9-17f (not airborne); good mid-range poke; Punish Counter puts opponent into limited juggle state (combos reliably into 236KK or SA2 unless whiff punishing a ranged attack); also causes limited juggle state on airborne Counter-hit (into 623HK at close range) and Punish Counter (slightly better juggles than grounded PC); extends hurtbox 1f before active that is vulnerable to projectiles; hitbox does not move forward during the active frames (cannot be spaced in neutral for better advantage)

elena.name: 蹲下轻拳 (2LP)
elena.notes: Chains into 2LP/2LK; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-6 is vulnerable only to aerial strikes (preventing its use as an anti-air); DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd active frame

elena.name: 蹲下中拳 (2MP)
elena.notes: Great cancelable poke in neutral; not an anti-air despite the animation; DR cancel is delayed until after active frames

elena.name: 蹲下重拳 (2HP)
elena.notes: 2 hits; Upper Body/Legs are anti-air invuln on frames 8-19 (solid anti-air but cannot hit cross-up); forces stand (important for 236K combo routes); 1st hit causes air reset when uses as an anti-air (2nd hit continues to whiff, leaving Elena with very little frame advantage when the opponent lands); 2nd hit puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (useful in DI or DR juggles where both hits connect); canceling anti-air 2HP into 236P sets up a juggle into the ~6MK follow-up if the opponent is juggled, or a safe meaty ~6LK if the opponent was air reset; cancel only comes out on the 2nd hit (will cancel on whiff if the first hit connects on airborne opponent); high pushback on hit; follow-up links require a Counter-hit, Punish Counter, Drive Rush starter into a ranged button; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage carries through both hits; if 1st hit is Perfect Parried, opponent can interrupt 2nd hit with 5f or faster attack

elena.name: 蹲下轻脚 (2LK)
elena.notes: Chains into 2LP/2LK

elena.name: 蹲下中脚 (2MK)
elena.notes: 2f extra recovery on whiff/block; good combo starter out of Drive Rush that leaves Elena +1 on block slightly out of throw range; moves Elena forward and can combo naturally into 2LP

elena.name: 蹲下重脚 (2HK)
elena.notes: Long range sweep; has juggle potential; punishable by most other sweeps even at max range

elena.name: 跳跃轻拳 (j.LP)
elena.notes: Cross-up; can be used as a fuzzy instant overhead (except vs. Blanka); Target Combo extension can lead to better advantage vs. grounded opponents, giving more time to hitconfirm a follow-up

elena.name: 跳跃中拳 (j.MP)
elena.notes: Puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; at most air-to-air timings, Elena's only follow-up juggle is a Target Combo extension; whiffs against standard-sized crouching opponents; lower body projectile invuln 8-17f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

elena.name: 跳跃重拳 (j.HP)
elena.notes: Elena's strongest overall jump-in (reaches downward faster than j.HK and deals all its damage in one hit); lower body projectile invuln 10-23f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

elena.name: 跳跃轻脚 (j.LK)
elena.notes: Can be used as a fuzzy instant overhead; good downward hitbox priority (likely to beat or trade with anti-airs)

elena.name: 跳跃中脚 (j.MK)
elena.notes: Cross-up with a wide hitbox in both directions; lower body projectile invuln 7-20f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

elena.name: 跳跃重脚 (j.HK)
elena.notes: 2 hits; 1st hit puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; 2nd hit causes spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; 2nd hit has the most horizontal range of Elena's air normals; overall weaker as an air approach due to the damage being split between 2 hits (very specific timing required to land both hits vs. grounded opponents); if 1st hit is stand blocked, the 2nd hit will not hit overhead against crouch block; lower body projectile invuln 10-22f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

elena.name: Trunk Slap 1
elena.notes: Forward-moving ranged poke that can be hitconfirmed into a TC knockdown follow-up; TC is always a true blockstring; pushback keeps Elena safe (except at close range vs. Marisa/E.Honda/Sagat 2LP and Zangief 2LK); pushback also prevents a follow-up link even with Drive Rush (+5), but can link 5LK after a corner Punish Counter

elena.name: Handstand Whip 1
elena.notes: Long-range overhead with fast startup and a hitconfirmable TC follow-up

elena.name: Round Arch
elena.notes: Low Crush 9-17f (not airborne); 2f extra recovery on whiff; Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts opponent into a limited juggle state (can chase with DR oki, 236LP~6LP~6LK pressure, or juggle 623MK/623KK if used point blank in the corner); Elena moves backward starting on frame 5 (can help avoid the opponent's attack or throw)

elena.name: Slide
elena.notes: 4f extra recovery on whiff or vs. armor; does not low profile under projectiles; reaches ~1/2 screen and is safe when spaced well

elena.name: Starling Beak
elena.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents (but can force stand with Punish Counter 5MP); interruptible 6-8f gap between hits; does not combo from the final 2 cancelable frames of 5MP without at least a Counter-hit

elena.name: Turning Tail
elena.notes: Whiffs on crouch blocking opponents; puts opponents into limited juggle state with a much more rewarding juggle after Punish Counter 5HP; if 5HP is stand blocked, the first hit of the follow-up will also be stand blocked, but the last hit still whiffs leaving Elena unsafe; starter scaling only applies if the 2nd HP begins the combo (e.g. opponent tries to jump out after crouch blocking 5HP)

elena.name: Hind Kick
elena.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state; Elena's main Target Combo conversion on crouching opponents; Special/DI/DR cancel is delayed until after 1st recovery frame

elena.name: Fluttering Lark
elena.notes: () refers to scaled damage from 2MK combo starter; whiffs on crouching opponents (-18 after 2MK on hit, -24 after 2MK on block); 4f extra recovery on whiff or parry; the HK itself usually cannot be blocked since a blocked 2MK forces the opponent to crouch under it, but the entire sequence can be parried (block data notated with * refers to this scenario); if the TC is delayed as late as possible, the opponent can block 2MK and then Parry the follow-up or get hit while trying to jump; Special/DI/DR cancel is delayed until after 1st recovery frame

elena.name: Trunk Slap 2
elena.notes: Hitconfirmable extension from long-range 6HP; has no juggle potential (will not juggle after DI wall splat); always a true blockstring from 6HP

elena.name: Trunk Slap 3
elena.notes: () refers to scaled damage after a 6HP combo starter; good corner carry and knockdown advantage that can lead to auto-timed Lynx Whirl pressure on the opponent's wakeup; always a true blockstring from 6HP~HP

elena.name: Handstand Whip 2
elena.notes: Hitconfirmable Target Combo that makes Elena's long-range overhead more threatening even without Drive Rush

elena.name: Soaring Raid
elena.notes: Can hit after cross-up j.LP; can be done from any jump direction; does not work as an air-to-air even after a Forced Knockdown; will not connect if the j.LP hits a crouching opponent

elena.name: Raptor Range
elena.notes: Knockdown ender from air-to-air j.MP that puts opponent into a limited juggle state; can be done from any jump direction; cannot connect on a grounded opponent

elena.name: Leg Tackle
elena.notes: Grants a frame-perfect throw loop against Zangief (Dash + walk 2f); allows a frame-perfect corner throw loop with Drive Rush (more lenient vs. Marisa/Blanka/E.Honda/Zangief); throw pressure is more effective when mixed with other DR buttons, or feints like DR~214P); can also Dash + 5MK for weak pressure and a link to 5LK on hit; Lynx Song can be used for mixups (LP Roll into 6LK/6MK to beat reversal buttons, OD Roll into 6HK to beat throws, empty LP Roll to bait Perfect Parry at only -4 on whiff); a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

elena.name: Leg Lift Throw
elena.notes: Side switches; no true throw oki even with Drive Rush (except frame-perfect DR~Throw vs. Zangief); in the corner, allows an auto-timed meaty DR~5MK that is +12 oH / +8 oB; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

elena.name: Giraffe Neck
elena.notes: See Drive Impact. Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

elena.name: Boar Charge (Block)
elena.notes: Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; see Drive Reversal.

elena.name: Boar Charge (Recovery)
elena.notes: Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze except for a 12f freeze when interacting with the opponent's throw hitbox (this also refunds 1 Drive bar after punishing the throw); see Drive Reversal.

elena.name: Drive Parry
elena.notes: See Drive Parry. Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

elena.name: Parry Drive Rush
elena.notes: See Drive Rush; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.548 (min/throw), 2.100 (min/block), 3.011 (max/final DR frame)

elena.name: Drive Rush Cancel
elena.notes: See Drive Rush; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

elena.name: LK Rhino Horn
elena.notes: Shortest distance; whiffs on crouching opponents; Low Crush 15-34f; puts opponents into limited juggle state with follow-ups possible in the corner; 3f extra recovery on block/whiff; KD Advantage refers to grounded hits (varies against airborne opponents)

elena.name: MK Rhino Horn
elena.notes: Medium distance; whiffs on crouching opponents; Low Crush 19-39f; puts opponents into limited juggle state with follow-ups possible in the corner; 4f extra recovery on block/whiff; KD Advantage refers to grounded hits (varies against airborne opponents)

elena.name: HK Rhino Horn
elena.notes: Farthest distance; whiffs on crouching opponents; Low Crush 23-43f; puts opponents into limited juggle state with follow-ups like 623HK possible in the corner; 4f extra recovery on block/whiff; KD Advantage refers to grounded hits (varies against airborne opponents)

elena.name: OD Rhino Horn
elena.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; Low Crush 13-35f; puts opponents into limited juggle state with follow-ups possible anywhere on the screen; some hits can whiff under high airborne opponents (at certain heights, allows a sideswitch juggle); 6f extra recovery on block/whiff; KD Advantage refers to grounded hits (varies against airborne opponents)

elena.name: LK Scratch Wheel
elena.notes: Strong close-range anti air but cannot hit cross-up; can launch high airborne opponent high enough for a follow-up Scratch Wheel juggle (incurs starter scaling)

elena.name: MK Scratch Wheel
elena.notes: Strong close/mid-range anti air but cannot hit cross-up; active frames 4-6 will only deal 1 hit for half damage, making early anti-air attempts weaker; can only incur starter scaling if trading with a grounded normal and landing a follow-up juggle

elena.name: HK Scratch Wheel
elena.notes: Strong mid-range anti air but cannot hit cross-up; has the most range for grounded juggles and cancels; connecting with active frames 3-4 makes the first hit whiff (500 less damage), and active frames 5-6 make the first 2 hits whiff (900 less damage), making early anti-air attempts weaker

elena.name: OD Scratch Wheel
elena.notes: Elena's primary reversal; cannot hit cross-up; connecting with active frames 5-6 makes the first hit whiff (450 less damage), making early anti-air attempts weaker

elena.name: LK Spinning Scythe
elena.notes: Lynx Whirl Cancels (on Hit/on Block/on PC): ~6LP -3/-12/+1, ~6MP -11/-20/-7, ~6HP -13/-22/-9; first 2 hits force stand (last 2 hits will whiff vs. crouch block); first 2 hits have an extended foot hurtbox that can only hit standing opponents (shorter range vs. crouching); block disadvantage refers to stand(crouch); 2nd hit is cancelable into Lynx Whirl (enhanced Roll) on hit/block (but not whiff); all follow-ups are interruptible on block (even if opponent is in Burnout); Lynx Whirl cancel allows Elena to keep up pressure, but does not naturally combo into the follow-ups; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage carries through first 2 hits (CH combos into ~6MK, PC combos into ~6LK); empty ~6LP Roll is safe on hit and can bait Parry/DI/Reversals; last hit puts opponent into limited juggle state (only SA3 cancel will combo unless 214LK connects in a high juggle)

elena.name: MK Spinning Scythe
elena.notes: Lynx Whirl Cancels (on Hit/on Block/on PC): ~6LP -3/-12/+1, ~6MP -11/-20/-7, ~6HP -13/-22/-9; first 2 hits force stand (last 2 hits will whiff vs. crouch block); first 2 hits have an extended foot hurtbox that can only hit standing opponents (shorter range vs. crouching); block disadvantage refers to stand(crouch); 2nd hit is cancelable into Lynx Whirl (enhanced Roll) on hit/block (but not whiff); all follow-ups are interruptible on block (even if opponent is in Burnout); Lynx Whirl cancel allows Elena to keep up pressure, but does not naturally combo into the follow-ups; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage carries through first 2 hits (CH combos into ~6MK, PC combos into ~6LK); empty ~6LP Roll is safe on hit and can bait Parry/DI/Reversals; last hit puts opponent into limited juggle state (only SA3 cancel will combo unless 214LK connects in a high juggle)

elena.name: HK Spinning Scythe
elena.notes: Lynx Whirl Cancels (on Hit/on Block/on PC): ~6LP -3/-12/+1, ~6MP -11/-20/-7, ~6HP -13/-22/-9; first 2 hits force stand (last 2 hits will whiff vs. crouch block); first 2 hits have an extended foot hurtbox that can only hit standing opponents (shorter range vs. crouching); block disadvantage refers to stand(crouch); 2nd hit is cancelable into Lynx Whirl (enhanced Roll) on hit/block (but not whiff); all follow-ups are interruptible on block (even if opponent is in Burnout); Lynx Whirl cancel allows Elena to keep up pressure, but does not naturally combo into the follow-ups; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage carries through first 2 hits (CH combos into ~6MK, PC combos into ~6LK); empty ~6LP Roll is safe on hit and can bait Parry/DI/Reversals; last hit puts opponent into limited juggle state, allowing follow-ups like 236MK, DR~2MP, SA2, canceled SA3, or corner 236LK~623HK

elena.name: OD Spinning Scythe
elena.notes: Lynx Whirl Cancels (on Hit/on Block/on PC): ~6LP -3/-10/+1, ~6MP -11/-18/-7, ~6HP -13/-20/-9; first 2 hits force stand (last 2 hits will whiff vs. crouch block); first 2 hits have an extended foot hurtbox that can only hit standing opponents (shorter range vs. crouching); block disadvantage refers to stand(crouch); 2nd hit is cancelable into Lynx Whirl (enhanced Roll) on hit/block (but not whiff); all follow-ups are interruptible on block (except ~6MK trades with 4f normals if the opponent is in Burnout); Lynx Whirl cancel allows Elena to keep up pressure, but does not naturally combo into the follow-ups; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage carries through first 2 hits (CH combos into ~6MK, PC combos into ~6LK); empty ~6LP Roll is safe on hit and can bait Parry/DI/Reversals; last hit puts opponent into limited juggle state, allowing follow-ups like 236MK, DR~2MP, SA2, canceled SA3, or corner 236LK~623HK

elena.name: LP Lynx Song
elena.notes: Shortest total distance (1.37); 13f/0.72 distance before 6LK; 16f/0.87 distance before 6MK/6HK/6P; crouch-sized hurtbox 3-26f (but still considered standing); can execute the 6LK follow-up 3f earlier than the other follow-ups; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration

elena.name: MP Lynx Song
elena.notes: Medium total distance (1.72); 13f/0.66 distance before 6LK; 18f/0.98 distance before 6MK/6HK/6P; crouch-sized hurtbox 3-26f (but still considered standing); can execute the 6LK follow-up 5f earlier than the other follow-ups; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration

elena.name: HP Lynx Song
elena.notes: Longest total distance (2.21); 16f/1.08 distance before 6LK; 19f/1.35 distance before 6MK/6HK/6P; crouch-sized hurtbox 3-26f (but still considered standing); can execute the 6LK follow-up 3f earlier than the other follow-ups; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration

elena.name: OD Lynx Song
elena.notes: Follow-ups are enhanced like the Lynx Whirl versions after only one spin; total distance is between the MP/HP versions (2.075); 15f/1.01 distance before 6LK; 18f/1.28 distance before 6MK/6HK/6P; crouch-sized hurtbox 3-26f (but still considered standing); can execute the 6LK follow-up 3f earlier than the other follow-ups; this version is good for combos, pressuring from neutral, and punishing projectiles due to the faster startup on enhanced follow-ups; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration

elena.name: LP Lynx Whirl
elena.notes: Accessible from a previous Lynx Song or Spin Scythe; performs an extra spin, enhancing the follow-up specials (~6LK, ~6MK, ~6HK); can continue rolling indefinitely with repeated ~6P inputs; crouch-sized hurtbox 1-26f (but still considered standing); startup refers to minimum number of frames before each follow-up can come out (15-21f ~6LK, 18-21f ~6MK/~6HK, 20-21f ~6P); total roll distance: 1.43; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration; safest version of empty Roll to cancel into (e.g. Spinning Scythe ~ empty Lynx Whirl to bait DI/Parry/reversal)

elena.name: MP Lynx Whirl
elena.notes: Accessible from a previous Lynx Song or Spin Scythe; performs an extra spin, enhancing the follow-up specials (~6LK, ~6MK, ~6HK); can continue rolling indefinitely with repeated ~6P inputs; crouch-sized hurtbox 1-26f (but still considered standing); startup refers to minimum number of frames before each follow-up can come out (15-21f ~6LK, 18-21f ~6MK/~6HK, 20-21f ~6P); total roll distance: 1.94; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration

elena.name: HP Lynx Whirl
elena.notes: Accessible from a previous Lynx Song or Spin Scythe; performs an extra spin, enhancing the follow-up specials (~6LK, ~6MK, ~6HK); can continue rolling indefinitely with repeated ~6P inputs; crouch-sized hurtbox 1-26f (but still considered standing); startup refers to minimum number of frames before each follow-up can come out (15-21f ~6LK, 18-21f ~6MK/~6HK, 20-21f ~6P); total roll distance: 2.46; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration

elena.name: OD Lynx Whirl
elena.notes: Nearly identical to meterless versions except that the cancel window into follow-up specials is extended 3f longer; accessible from a previous OD Lynx Song; performs an extra spin, enhancing the follow-up specials (~6LK, ~6MK, ~6HK); can continue rolling indefinitely with repeated ~6P inputs; crouch-sized hurtbox 1-26f (but still considered standing); startup refers to minimum number of frames before each follow-up can come out (15-24f ~6LK, 18-24f ~6MK/~6HK, 20-24f ~6P); total roll distance: 2.59; Elena is in a Counter-hit state for the entire roll duration

elena.name: Leopard Snap
elena.notes: Elena immediately loses crouch-sized hurtbox and projectile invuln from Lynx Song (hard to use vs. projectiles); generally safe on block if spaced as a poke; punishable by most characters at closer ranges (notable exceptions: A.K.I. only gets 2LK, Mai gets nothing); combos when buffered from 2MP or 2MK~HK in neutral; puts the opponent into a limited juggle state (only into SA3 cancel except in high corner juggles); total minimum startup depends on which strength of Lynx Song was used (LP 13+10, MP 13+10, HP 16+10)

elena.name: OD Leopard Snap
elena.notes: Elena immediately loses crouch-sized hurtbox and projectile invuln from Lynx Song (hard to use vs. projectiles); strong ender from Spinning Scythe on hit (3f gap) to reset pressure (but does not frame trap on block); useful for pressure on block (can beat 4f normals with 2LP, catch back walk with 2LK~2LP, and throw except vs. midscreen back walk); 1f extra recovery on whiff; the version used from OD Lynx Song is not considered an OD move for cancel purposes (no SA2 cancel); puts the opponent into a limited juggle state; total minimum startup from OD Lynx Song is 15+10 (longer and variable when used from Lynx Whirl)

elena.name: Harvest Circle
elena.notes: Feet/leg hurtboxes are anti-air invuln while active on frames 8-10 (both the kicking leg and the topmost body hurtbox); can anti-air opponents jumping out of roll pressure, but cannot hit cross-up; maintains projectile invuln from Lynx Song to counter fireballs more effectively; Elena immediately loses crouch-sized hurtbox from Lynx Song; total minimum startup depends on which strength of Lynx Song was used (LP 16+8, MP 18+8, HP 19+8); puts opponent into a limited juggle state

elena.name: OD Harvest Circle
elena.notes: 2f extra recovery on block/whiff; 1st hit pulls opponents inward on hit/block for combo consistency; feet/leg hurtboxes are anti-air invuln while active on frames 8-10 (both the kicking leg and the topmost body hurtbox); can anti-air opponents jumping out of roll pressure, but cannot hit cross-up; maintains projectile invuln from Lynx Song/Whirl to counter fireballs more effectively; Elena immediately loses crouch-sized hurtbox from Lynx Song; can combo from Spinning Scythe ~ Lynx Whirl on Counter-hit/Punish Counter; puts opponent into a limited juggle state; total minimum startup from OD Lynx Song is 18+8 (longer and variable when used from Lynx Whirl)

elena.name: Mallet Smash
elena.notes: Low Crush 14-24f (final active frame is considered standing but still has a high hurtbox); projectile invuln disappears for a brief period after Lynx Song (less effective as a fireball counter); projectile invuln does not apply to the top of Elena's head; Elena immediately loses crouch-sized hurtbox from Lynx Song; safe overhead that can lead to a 5MK combo after baiting the opponent's throw tech; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state on hit (can always pick up corner juggles, but midscreen juggles depend on height/spacing); total minimum startup depends on which strength of Lynx Song was used (LP 16+22, MP 18+22, HP 19+22)

elena.name: OD Mallet Smash
elena.notes: 2 hits (if 1st hit is blocked, 2nd hit is no longer an overhead); Low Crush 5-22f (can avoid moves before becoming airborne); projectile invuln disappears for a brief period after Lynx Song/Whirl (less effective as a fireball counter); projectile invuln does not apply to the top of Elena's head; Elena immediately loses crouch-sized hurtbox from Lynx Song; overhead that gives strong follow-up pressure on block, a 2LP on hit, and a medium combo after baiting the opponent's low buttons or throw tech; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state on hit (can always pick up a juggle, but exact route depends on height and distance); total minimum startup from OD Lynx Song is 18+22 (longer and variable when used from Lynx Whirl)

elena.name: LP Moon Glider
elena.notes: Forces stand; sways back slightly (can avoid attacks); sways on frames 5-14 (max distance of 0.40 on frame 5); puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; safe option out of Drive Rush that can bait the opponent's button/throw and grants a light combo extension after a whiff punish

elena.name: MP Moon Glider
elena.notes: Forces stand; sways back a moderate distance (can avoid attacks); sways on frames 5-18 (max distance of 0.50 on frame 9); puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; safe option out of Drive Rush that can bait the opponent's button/throw and grants a 5MK combo extension after a whiff punish

elena.name: HP Moon Glider
elena.notes: Forces stand; sways back significantly (can avoid attacks); sways on frames 5-23 (max distance of 0.71 on frames 14-16); puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; safe option out of Drive Rush that can bait the opponent's button/throw and grants a 5MK combo extension after a whiff punish

elena.name: OD Moon Glider
elena.notes: Forces stand; sways back a moderate distance (can avoid attacks); sways on frames 5-19 (max distance of 0.56 on frame 9); puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; safe option out of Drive Rush that can bait the opponent's button/throw and grants a light combo extension after a whiff punish

elena.name: Moon Glider Follow-up
elena.notes: Hitconfirmable follow-up from safe sway starter; puts opponents into limited juggle state (into SA3)

elena.name: OD Moon Glider Follow-up
elena.notes: Hitconfirmable follow-up from safe sway starter; puts opponents into limited juggle state (into SA2/SA3); sets up a safe jump vs. grounded opponents near the corner

elena.name: SA: Meteor Volley
elena.notes: Good anti-air with air invuln that fully covers the first 2 hits; cannot be used as an invincible reversal against grounded strikes/throws/projectiles (making it much more dangerous to be in Burnout); cannot hit cross-up; puts opponents into limited juggle state (can combo a 236KK full connect after a grounded hit); extreme block disadvantage allows many characters to set activate installs without sacrificing optimal punish starters

elena.name: SA: Revival Dance
elena.notes: Excellent anti-fireball tool due to its invincibility and forward movement; slow startup makes it risky as a reversal (can be safely meatied by light normals); leaves Elena farther away than the Healing version, but with more advantage for Lynx Song or Drive Rush pressure; generally a poor anti-air but can catch some mid-range neutral jumps or divekick landing recovery; has a large combo-only hitbox that makes it more consistent in juggles; opponents can jump after the Super freeze to avoid a chip KO

elena.name: SA: Revival Dance (Healing)
elena.notes: Sacrifices damage and oki in exchange for healing 100 HP; the healing amount is not affected by damage scaling, making it more useful in a highly scaled combo; Elena builds 1 bar of Drive gauge when healing which also allows Drive regeneration to resume slightly earlier (also applies to Burnout gauge); excellent anti-fireball tool due to its invincibility and forward movement; slow startup makes it risky as a reversal (can be safely meatied by light normals); opponents can jump after the Super freeze to avoid a chip KO

elena.name: SA: Song of the Grasslands
elena.notes: Cinematic time regenerates ~2.1 Drive bars for Elena; large combo-only hitbox makes it more consistent in juggles; reliable but expensive reversal when in Burnout; very consistent anti-air at mid to long range, but cannot hit cross-up and can whiff under closer jumps; opponents cannot avoid a chip KO by jumping after the Super freeze

elena.name: SA: Song of the Grasslands (CA)
elena.notes: Available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~2.1 Drive bars for Elena; large combo-only hitbox makes it more consistent in juggles; reliable but expensive reversal when in Burnout; very consistent anti-air at mid to long range, but cannot hit cross-up and can whiff under closer jumps; opponents cannot avoid a chip KO by jumping after the Super freeze

elena.name: Neutral Taunt
elena.notes: "It's such a lovely day. And I hope you're having a good one too!"

elena.name: Forward Taunt
elena.notes: "One, two, and spin! What do you say? How about you dance with me!"; overrides the current background music with the Reniala Remains stage theme with increased volume

elena.name: Back Taunt
elena.notes: "And up!"; can hold forward or back to transition into a hand-walking animation on frames 181-370

elena.name: Back Taunt ~ Forward Walk
elena.notes: "Cool right? Give it a try!"; cannot change walk animation once it has begun; total animation time depends on when Forward was input during the initial Back Taunt

elena.name: Back Taunt ~ Back Walk
elena.notes: "Hehe, over here!"; cannot change walk animation once it has begun; total animation time depends on when Back was input during the initial Back Taunt

elena.name: Down Taunt
elena.notes: "What's up?"

sagat.name: 站立轻拳 (5LP)
sagat.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; great range for a chainable 5f jab (but slightly shorter than a standard shoto 5LK); DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd recovery frame; Sagat's only light normal that combos naturally into 214LK

sagat.name: 站立中拳 (5MP)
sagat.notes: Core pressure tool for frame traps (5MPx2 sets up a trade combo vs. most reversal 4f normals); pushback on block is too far for a throw mixup without Drive Rush; links consistently into 2MP on counter-hit or into 5HK on Punish Counter (very strong Drive Reversal punish option); on regular hit can lead to 5MP, 5MP, 5LP combo

sagat.name: 站立重拳 (5HP)
sagat.notes: 3f extra recovery on whiff; huge range poke with a hitconfirmable TC follow-up; the first 10 recovery frames extend a wide arm-height hurtbox making it easily whiff punished by standing normals

sagat.name: 站立轻脚 (5LK)
sagat.notes: Long range but slow startup (more comparable to a medium normal); 2f extra recovery on whiff; great whiff punish tool that combos consistently into 623HP on Punish Counter; input overlap with 6LK Low Step Kick makes it harder to walk forward and poke in neutral; DR cancel is delayed until after 3rd recovery frame

sagat.name: 站立中脚 (5MK)
sagat.notes: Very long poke with a semi-hitconfirmable TC follow-up; more range vs. standing opponents (the tip of the hitbox whiffs on crouching opponents); the first 10 recovery frames extend a wide leg hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by standing normals; extends a wider body hurtbox for the entire whiff recovery

sagat.name: 站立重脚 (5HK)
sagat.notes: Upper Body/Leg hurtbox is anti-air invincible on frames 9-15 (solid anti-air against midrange jumps); cannot hit cross-up; 1st hit forces stand on hit; 2nd hit whiffs on crouching opponents (2f worse on block); 4f extra recovery if both hits whiff; 1st hit deals extra hitstun, allowing a natural combo into 214HK; deals full damage / Drive damage / Meter gain even if only the 2nd hit connects; 1st hit puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state (limited juggle if comboed from a wallsplat or airborne crumple), then air resets on the 2nd hit; 2nd hit only has juggle potential after the 1st hit connects; the first 11 recovery frames extend a wide leg hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by standing normals; carries counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits

sagat.name: 蹲下轻拳 (2LP)
sagat.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; excellent range for a 4f jab; high pushback makes tick throw and counter-hit pressure weaker, but also allows Sagat to space himself outside the opponent's reversal normals on block; DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd recovery frame (up to the 3rd recovery frame); topmost hurtbox on frames 1-5 is vulnerable only to aerial strikes (preventing its use as an anti-air)

sagat.name: 蹲下中拳 (2MP)
sagat.notes: Solid mid-range cancelable poke and buffer tool; 1f extra recovery on block; 3f extra recovery on whiff; significantly more range on active frames 2-3 (more effective linking from +8 or punishing -8 moves); cancelable into 2 different Target Combo follow-ups with different hitconfirm timings (requires Punish Counter or Drive Rush for 2MP~HP combo); topmost hurtbox is vulnerable only to aerial strikes on frames 1-9 (preventing its use as an anti-air), and is projectile invincible on frames 1-14 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 15-26 are still vulnerable)

sagat.name: 蹲下重拳 (2HP)
sagat.notes: Very long range for a cancelable and hitconfirmable poke; significantly more range on active frames 3-4; topmost hurtbox is vulnerable only to aerial strikes on frames 1-14 (preventing its use as an anti-air), and is projectile invincible on frames 1-19 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 20-35 are still vulnerable)

sagat.name: 蹲下轻脚 (2LK)
sagat.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; low starter that can combo into any 3-light chain from close range

sagat.name: 蹲下中脚 (2MK)
sagat.notes: Amazing hitbox priority as a neutral poke; can link to 5LP at closer ranges, or into 2MP/5LK on Counter-hit; useful combo/pressure starter out of Drive Rush (but has poor link options near its max range)

sagat.name: 蹲下重脚 (2HK)
sagat.notes: Has some juggle potential; great range and hitbox priority; can be punished on block by most other sweeps in the game

sagat.name: 跳跃轻拳 (j.LP)
sagat.notes: Fast air-to-air with solid horizontal range

sagat.name: 跳跃中拳 (j.MP)
sagat.notes: 2 hits; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; if 1st hit is stand blocked, the 2nd hit will not hit overhead against crouch block; lower body projectile invuln 8-22f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

sagat.name: 跳跃重拳 (j.HP)
sagat.notes: Strong downward attack angle; spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; lower body projectile invuln 10-22f (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

sagat.name: 跳跃轻脚 (j.LK)
sagat.notes: Cross-up; can be used as a fuzzy instant overhead

sagat.name: 跳跃中脚 (j.MK)
sagat.notes: Long horizontal range (barely shorter than j.HK) with a better downward attack angle and nearly identical hitstun and blockstun; lower body projectile invuln 8-25f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

sagat.name: 跳跃重脚 (j.HK)
sagat.notes: Longest horizontal range; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; lower body projectile invuln 10-21f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

sagat.name: Tiger Heavy Elbow
sagat.notes: Spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; Drive Rush gives a combo into 2MP (no real strike/throw pressure on block); meaty timing allows a follow-up link (up to +5/0 on final active frame)

sagat.name: Tiger Monolith
sagat.notes: Tall hitbox on 2nd hit, but also extends a tall hurtbox with no anti-air invincibility (likely to lose/trade with jump-ins); cannot hit cross-up; 2nd hit whiffs on crouch blocking opponents (3f worse on block and not cancelable); cancel does not occur until the 2nd hit's active frames (still executes on hit even if the 2nd hit whiffs); puts opponents into a limited juggle state (can combo into 236MP, DR~delay 4HP > 236HK, 623MP for great midscreen damage and corner carry); free juggle state from DR~4HP, allowing a more optimal corner juggle: > 214MK, 4HP > 236HK, 623MP; launches higher on Counter-hit/Punish Counter (KD +41) or on airborne opponents (KD +40); 1st hit puts opponent into a free juggle OTG bounce state that is usually overwritten by the 2nd hit (but can still occur on trades or when hitting extended hurtboxes)

sagat.name: Low Step Kick
sagat.notes: Long range advancing low poke that leaves Sagat close for a strike/throw mixup on hit while remaining safe on block; 3f extra recovery on whiff; can link into light normals on Counter-hit, or into 2MP after Drive Rush or Punish Counter; knocks down airborne opponents (KD +35~38) when juggled into (but has no juggle potential on its own); the first 7 recovery frames extend a wide foot hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by low-reaching normals

sagat.name: High Step Kick
sagat.notes: Upper Body/Leg hurtbox is anti-air invincible on frames 14-19 (useful as a predictive long range anti-air); whiffs on crouching opponents; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Punish Counter staggers grounded opponents and puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state; 3f fewer total frames on block/parry/armor (active frames end upon contact, with variable recovery depending on which active frame connected); the first 5 recovery frames extend a wide hurtbox where the kicking leg was (too high for many attacks to easily connect as a whiff punish); extends hurtbox 1f before active that is vulnerable to projectiles; useful in Drive Rush cancel routes from 2HP/5HK/2MP~HP (but the pushback prevents Sagat's usual midscreen link of 4HP > 236MP, juggle DR~4HP)

sagat.name: Middle Step Kick
sagat.notes: Always a true blockstring even at max delay; somewhat hitconfirmable knockdown from a very strong midrange poke; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (can combo 623LP after DI wallsplat on hit)

sagat.name: Tiger Sting
sagat.notes: Both hits are always a true blockstring; hitconfirmable knockdown from a very strong midrange poke; sets up a KD +42 safe jump when juggled into (like after a DI wallsplat on hit/block)

sagat.name: Tiger Slash
sagat.notes: Combos after Punish Counter or Drive Rush 2MP only; () refers to scaled damage after 2MP combo starter; causes limited juggle OTG bounce vs. airborne opponents

sagat.name: Tiger Rise
sagat.notes: 3f blockstring gap between hits; () refers to scaled damage after 2MP combo starter; harder to confirm into from 2MP but combos naturally; launch only allows a canceled Super but no other follow-up juggles; easily hitconfirmed into Super even if only the 2nd hit connects as a frame trap; higher KD advantage when juggled into

sagat.name: Tiger Hang
sagat.notes: Can use Drive Rush for a corner throw loop with 4f timing on standard characters; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

sagat.name: Tiger Carry
sagat.notes: Side switch; no true oki after throwing opponent into the corner, but can pressure with Tiger Shot, MK/HK Knee, or spaced Drive Rush normals; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

sagat.name: Tiger Punishment
sagat.notes: See Drive Impact. Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

sagat.name: Tiger Twin Babel (Block)
sagat.notes: Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; see Drive Reversal.

sagat.name: Tiger Twin Babel (Recovery)
sagat.notes: Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze except for a 12f freeze when interacting with the opponent's throw hitbox (this also refunds 1 Drive bar after punishing the throw); see Drive Reversal.

sagat.name: Drive Parry
sagat.notes: See Drive Parry. Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

sagat.name: Parry Drive Rush
sagat.notes: See Drive Rush; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.546 (min/throw), 1.869 (min/block), 3.156 (max/final DR frame)

sagat.name: Drive Rush Cancel
sagat.notes: See Drive Rush; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

sagat.name: LP Low Tiger Shot
sagat.notes: Fast 1-hit projectile (speed is not variable); can hit crouching opponents unlike MP/HP High Tiger Shot; has extremely long recovery compared to most projectiles (more vulnerable to jumps, Drive Impact, projectile invuln moves, and Perfect Parry + Drive Rush); the projectile travels low to the ground, preventing many low profile attacks from avoiding it (e.g. Kimberly's slide, A.K.I.'s Sinister Slide); Sagat is in a crouching state for the entire move duration with crouch-sized hurtboxes; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 16-43 and a leg hurtbox on frames 14-50; topmost hurtboxes are vulnerable only to air attacks on frames 1-50 (more vulnerable to jump-ins despite crouching) and are projectile invincible on frames 1-31 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 32-50 are still vulnerable)

sagat.name: OD Low Tiger Shot
sagat.notes: Fast 2-hit OD projectile; can hit crouching opponents; can be used while a meterless Tiger Shot is still on-screen; the projectile travels low to the ground, preventing many low profile attacks from avoiding it (e.g. Kimberly's slide, A.K.I.'s Sinister Slide); Sagat is in a crouching state for the entire move duration with crouch-sized hurtboxes; puts opponents into a limited juggle state; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 16-37 and a leg hurtbox on frames 12-44; topmost hurtboxes are vulnerable only to air attacks on frames 1-44 (more vulnerable to jump-ins despite crouching) and are projectile invincible on frames 1-29 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 30-44 are still vulnerable); starter scaling does not apply if only the 2nd hit connects (e.g. clashing with 1-hit OD fireball or breaking Drive Impact armor)

sagat.name: MP High Tiger Shot
sagat.notes: Medium speed 1-hit projectile (comparable to a shoto HP fireball, but much slower than Sagat's other projectiles); whiffs on crouching opponents unless they extend an upward hurtbox; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (useful juggle tool after 4HP launch); has much better recovery and frame advantage than the Low version; can be used meaty on the opponent's wakeup even if they crouch block, but the opponent can input a crouching button to avoid blocking the projectile; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 18-32 and a leg hurtbox on frames 18-42

sagat.name: HP High Tiger Shot
sagat.notes: Fast 1-hit projectile; whiffs on crouching opponents unless they extend an upward hurtbox; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; has much better recovery and frame advantage than the Low version; can be used meaty on the opponent's wakeup even if they crouch block, but the opponent can input a crouching button to avoid blocking the projectile; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 14-28 and a leg hurtbox on frames 14-42

sagat.name: OD High Tiger Shot
sagat.notes: Extremely fast 3-hit OD projectile; slow startup but very powerful in fireball wars once released; can hit crouching opponents unlike the MP/HP High Tiger Shots; can be used while a meterless Tiger Shot is still on-screen; excellent frame advantage on hit or block; puts opponents into a limited juggle state; can juggle into SA1 from anywhere on the screen, and into another OD High Tiger Shot from fullscreen (or at close range vs. cornered opponents); extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 25-41 and a leg hurtbox on frames 25-48; starter scaling does not apply if only the 3rd hit connects (e.g. clashing with 2-hit OD fireball or breaking Drive Impact armor)

sagat.name: LP Tiger Uppercut
sagat.notes: Sagat's primary anti-air with fast startup but short range; deals 300 less damage on active frames 4-10; cannot hit cross-up; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

sagat.name: MP Tiger Uppercut
sagat.notes: Much more range than LP version for mid-range anti airs and more consistent cancels from light normals; much slower startup (limits usefulness in many juggles); forward movement makes Sagat more likely to whiff under an opponent's jump-in; deals 600 less damage on active frames 4-10; cannot hit cross-up; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

sagat.name: HP Tiger Uppercut
sagat.notes: Extremely long range but slow startup (cannot combo naturally from light normals, but works well as a combo ender from 5LK whiff punish); deals 600 less damage on active frames 3-10; cannot hit cross-up; can be charged into a much stronger version by holding the button 24 frames; releasing the button early results in uncharged 623HP with 8f startup after release; if partially charged, the Air Invuln is 1-9f then 1-11f after the button is released, and the airborne frames are 12-57f after the button is released; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

sagat.name: HP Tiger Uppercut (Hold)
sagat.notes: Button must be held 24f for fully charged version; causes a wall splat on hit that leaves Sagat at a fixed distance (no follow-up combo); deals 1100 less damage on active frames 4-10 with no wallsplat animation (KD +29 on active frame 4); cannot hit cross-up; 1st hit puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-3 only)

sagat.name: OD Tiger Uppercut
sagat.notes: Sagat's main reversal; slightly slower than most OD reversals (can be safejabbed by Dee Jay 5LP but is otherwise reliable); deals less damage if it connects on later active frames (1st hit deals significant portion of overall damage); cannot hit cross-up

sagat.name: LK Tiger Knee Crush
sagat.notes: Shortest horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 10-12 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +2) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it always connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents

sagat.name: MK Tiger Knee Crush
sagat.notes: Medium horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 14-15 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +3) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 4 active frames connect); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents; sets up midscreen safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

sagat.name: HK Tiger Knee Crush
sagat.notes: Furthest horizontal distance; much better block advantage when spaced at max range; 2nd hit active frames 1-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first hit whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+4 on block); if the 1st hit is crouch blocked, opponent cannot switch to stand block the 2nd hit; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 6 active frames connect, or 623MP / SA2 if the final active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; Sweet Spot occurs when juggling into the 3rd or 4th active frame, dealing 1300 damage (single hit) with a higher spinning juggle launch (ensures a follow-up juggle is possible even midscreen); the 2nd hit's extended Knee hitbox is too high to connect on standing characters on active frames 2-7 (tall characters: active frames 4-6); sets up corner safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

sagat.name: OD Tiger Knee Crush
sagat.notes: 1st hit transitions to a different follow-up on hit, resulting in higher damage and a tumbling +66 knockdown (allows a 623LP juggle in the corner); if 1st hit whiffs, the next 2 hits deal 500 damage each and give a worse knockdown (only 1 hit at farthest ranges); safe on block but usually lands inside the opponent's throw range; 2nd hit active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out, it connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+1 on block); unlike HK Knee, the opponent can switch to stand block after the first hit connects, leaving Sagat at -2; blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; later hits put opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP)

sagat.name: LK Tiger Nexus
sagat.notes: 1f extra recovery vs. armor (DI is a guaranteed punish if not canceled to SA3); the only strength of 214K that can combo naturally from 5LP (3-light confirm can reach if point blank, but results in weaker mixup from ~6LK ender); does not frame trap when canceled on block (except from Light normals with Drive Rush or Burnout); combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214LK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214LK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

sagat.name: MK Tiger Nexus
sagat.notes: 1f extra recovery vs. armor (DI is a guaranteed punish if not canceled to SA3); combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; 214MK combos from canceled 2MP/2HP/5HK (these cancels also frame trap on block); cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; lacks natural juggle potential but can juggle after DR~4HP (free juggle state) for a powerful 1-bar corner combo (DR~4HP > 214MK, 4HP > 236HK, 623MP); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214MK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214MK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

sagat.name: HK Tiger Nexus
sagat.notes: Slow startup, only combos naturally from the first hit of 5HK (requires Drive Rush or Punish Counter to combo from 2HP, 4HP launch, or 5HK 2nd hit); 214HK cannot frame trap when canceled from a normal (except for Burnout + Drive Rush into 2MP/2HP/5HK); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; can juggle after DR~4HP (easier execution but less damaging than his MP Tiger Shot juggle sequence); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214HK)

sagat.name: OD Tiger Nexus
sagat.notes: Similar to HK version but faster (can cancel from more starters like 2HP, 4HP launch, and 5HK 2nd hit); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214KK)

sagat.name: Mighty Tiger
sagat.notes: Mixup tool that is unsafe on block; the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; safe vs. Burnout but no longer frame traps (unless the 6LK input is delayed from 214LK/MK); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (e.g. after Counter-hit 214LK/MK); causes immediate knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter; loses to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214LK/MK (but safe after 214HK unless the 6LK input is delayed); if used from a 2-light chain, opponent is in range for Throw or 2LK~5LP chain (too far if starting with 3-light chain)

sagat.name: OD Mighty Tiger
sagat.notes: Mixup tool that is safe on block; +1 vs. Burnout (but no longer frame traps and has no real looping pressure); the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; puts opponents into limited juggle OTG bounce state on counter-hit or airborne hit (KD +47, can juggle into 623MP, SA2, SA3, 2HK, or 236LPMP which combos to SA1 in the corner); safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK unless the 6LK input is delayed

sagat.name: Greedy Tiger
sagat.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (only allows 623LP/PP juggle in the corner, or 623MP from CH/PC 214LK/MK launch); frame data vs. crouch from 214LK/214MK: -19 oH / -26 oB / KD +51 onPC launch; frame data vs. crouch from 214HK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC (214HK keeps opponent crouching on Punish Counter); safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214K; 5f blockstring gap after 214LK/MK (loses to reversal standing/crouching 4f normals); 3f blockstring gap after 214HK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

sagat.name: OD Greedy Tiger
sagat.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (no midscreen juggle besides SA2/SA3 cancel); in the corner, can juggle into 623MP/PP, 2HK, or SA2 from a grounded hit, in addition to 236LK, 236LPMP, SA1, or SA3 on an airborne connect (e.g. 4HP launch or DI wallsplat); frame data vs. crouch from 214KK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC; safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK; 3f blockstring gap after 214KK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

sagat.name: Nova Tiger
sagat.notes: Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; only combos naturally from 214HK (requires juggle state for LK/MK versions, like a CH/PC Tiger Nexus); after blocked 214LK/MK, interruptible 9f blockstring gap (5f gap vs. Burnout, loses to 4f normals); after blocked 214HK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214HK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

sagat.name: OD Nova Tiger
sagat.notes: Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; combos naturally from 214KK; after blocked 214KK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214KK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

sagat.name: SA: Tiger Cannon
sagat.notes: 8-hit Super projectile; can be used while OD Tiger Shot is on-screen (but not meterless Tiger Shot); fast travel speed allows it to be used in long range juggles; projectile speed is not affected by button strength

sagat.name: SA: Savage Tiger
sagat.notes: Goes into one of 4 follow-ups after frame 76 on hit (depending on which direction is held while clutching the opponent); Sagat's best reversal Super (but is still slow enough to be baited by an opponent's safejab setup); can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; Sagat has travel time throughout the active frames (takes longer than SA3 to reach full range)

sagat.name:
SA: Savage Tiger Raid
(Damage)
sagat.notes: Highest damage variant of SA2; leaves the opponent far away with no oki; has significant corner carry (over 1/2 screen)

sagat.name:
SA: Savage Tiger Zenith
(Launcher)
sagat.notes: Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state (juggle counter is always set to 2 regardless of previous juggle state); Hard Knockdown if the opponent hits the ground instead of being juggled; useful for corner carry, building back some Super gauge, and getting a good mix of damage + oki (but usually results in less damage than Tiger Raid)

sagat.name:
SA: Savage Tiger Pendulum
(Side Switch)
sagat.notes: Switches sides with opponent; leaves the opponent far away with no oki

sagat.name:
SA: Savage Tiger Stomp
(Oki)
sagat.notes: Leaves the opponent close to Sagat for stronger oki than other versions; can walk up for a strike/throw/shimmy mixup; gives enough advantage for an immediate 6MP overhead

sagat.name: SA: Tiger Vanquisher
sagat.notes: Cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

sagat.name: SA: Tiger Vanquisher (CA)
sagat.notes: Available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

sagat.name: Neutral Taunt
sagat.notes: "If you desire the throne, stand tall against the emperor."

sagat.name: Forward Taunt
sagat.notes: "The emperor's strength is peerless. However, it would be my pleasure to test your strength!"

sagat.name: Back Taunt
sagat.notes: "If you're on a path to attain strength, show me your worth!"

cviper.name: 站立轻拳 (5LP)
cviper.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; 214HP Feint cancel: -4 oH / -10 oB; more range than 2LP but worse advantage on hit/block

cviper.name: 站立中拳 (5MP)
cviper.notes: Primary combo and frame trap starter; 214HP Feint cancel: +3 oH / -2 oB

cviper.name: 站立重拳 (5HP)
cviper.notes: Long range poke that can be converted into damaging combos with High Jump cancel into Feint or Seismo; HJC~214HP Feint cancel: +6 oH / +1 oB

cviper.name: 站立轻脚 (5LK)
cviper.notes: Primary 5f punish tool; higher hitstun than other lights (can combo into 214MP); links from 2LP allowing C.Viper to combo 4 light normals; DR cancel is delayed until after active frames; 214HP Feint cancel: -2 oH / -7 oB

cviper.name: 站立中脚 (5MK)
cviper.notes: Strong poke that can combo into specials with a High Jump cancel (214HP can whiff at farther ranges); can link into SA2 on counter-hit from around the max range of 2MP; 2f extra recovery on whiff; HJC~214HP Feint cancel: +5 oH / -3 oB

cviper.name: 站立重脚 (5HK)
cviper.notes: Staggers opponent on Punish Counter; shorter range vs. crouching opponents; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle OTG bounce that can be followed up with High Jump cancel into Thunder Dash, OD Burning Kick, or any Super; can be juggled into after Seismo > HJC Air Burning Kick, then High Jump canceled into more damage; extends a hurtbox 1f before active that is vulnerable to projectiles; HJC~214HP Feint cancel: +7 oH / 0 oB / +22 onPC; HJC~214K~Dash cancel onPC: +8 meterless / +11 OD; strict 2f timing to input HJC into grounded Burning Kick (cannot be buffered on the first frame of High Jump)

cviper.name: 蹲下轻拳 (2LP)
cviper.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd active frame; 214HP Feint cancel: -3 oH / -9 oB; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-6 is vulnerable only to aerial attacks, preventing its use as an anti-air

cviper.name: 蹲下中拳 (2MP)
cviper.notes: High hitstun for a medium normal (combos into OD Seismo); special/DI/High Jump cancel is delayed until after 2nd active frame; 214HP Feint cancel: +5 oH / -2 oB; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-8 is vulnerable only to aerial attacks, preventing its use as an anti-air

cviper.name: 蹲下重拳 (2HP)
cviper.notes: C.Viper's main cancelable poke (no High Jump cancel required) that combos into meterless Seismic Hammer; forces stand on hit; 214HP Feint cancel: +6 oH / -1 oB

cviper.name: 蹲下轻脚 (2LK)
cviper.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; can be High Jump canceled allowing for stronger combo options than most 2LKs; can input High Jump Cancel without returning to neutral for easier execution; HJC~214HP Feint cancel: -6 oH / -11 oB

cviper.name: 蹲下中脚 (2MK)
cviper.notes: Amazing range for a low poke that can lead to combos with High Jump cancel; can input High Jump Cancel without returning to neutral for easier execution; HJC~214HP Feint cancel: +4 oH / -2 oB

cviper.name: 蹲下重脚 (2HK)
cviper.notes: 4f extra recovery on block; C. Viper's only standard normal that cannot be High Jump canceled; has some juggle potential; Punish Counter sets up a safe jump using High Jump (fairly impractical outside the corner, as a forward High Jump usually sails over the opponent)

cviper.name: 跳跃轻拳 (j.LP)
cviper.notes: Forces stand on hit; short range air-to-air with an upward angle

cviper.name: 跳跃中拳 (j.MP)
cviper.notes: Puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; cancelable into Aerial Burning Kick on forward or neutral jump; lower body projectile invuln 8-22f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

cviper.name: 跳跃重拳 (j.HP)
cviper.notes: Spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; forces stand on hit; good hitbox for vertical approaches; lower body projectile invuln 11-23f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

cviper.name: 跳跃轻脚 (j.LK)
cviper.notes: Can be used as a fuzzy instant overhead; strong hitbox priority; against tall standing characters, can combo any close range button into High Jump canceled j.LK on the way up

cviper.name: 跳跃中脚 (j.MK)
cviper.notes: Cross-up; strong overall jump-in (great hitbox priority and the most range of her forward jump normals); lower body projectile invuln 7-20f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

cviper.name: 跳跃重脚 (j.HK)
cviper.notes: Cross-up; cancelable into Aerial Burn Kick (only combos naturally into HK/OD version on grounded opponents, and cannot juggle after air-to-air connect due to air reset); cancelable until the 37th airborne frame of a forward jump or High Jump; lower body projectile invuln 8-19f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

cviper.name: 垂直跳跃重脚 (8HK)
cviper.notes: Longest horizontal range of Viper's air normals; in the corner or against wide characters (Blanka/E.Honda/Zangief), can combo Punish Counter 5HK into High Jump cancel nj.HK for powerful combo extension; lower body projectile invuln 10-19f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

cviper.name: Viper Elbow
cviper.notes: 16-27f Low Crush (not airborne or throw invincible)

cviper.name: Double Kick
cviper.notes: 2 hits; carries counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; if 1st hit is Perfect Parried, opponent can interrupt 2nd hit with 16f or faster attack; useful approach tool from Drive Rush (strike/throw mixup on block, 2MP link on hit); can be spaced effectively in neutral to keep C.Viper out of the opponent's throw range on block

cviper.name: High Impulse
cviper.notes: Grants a corner throw loop by walking or dashing (+7, requires delayed throw); can pressure with MK Burning Kick (+2 oB, DI-safe), MK Burning Kick ~ Double Burn (also +2 oB, true blockstring, gives better Drive damage but the sequence loses to wakeup DI), or HK Burning Kick ~ Double Burn (leaves a small blockstring gap between hits, allowing C. Viper to land and counter-DI); a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

cviper.name: Thunder Cradle
cviper.notes: Side switch; can pressure with Drive Rush after a corner side switch (but cannot beat reversal 4f normals with another throw); meaty LK Burning Kick can lead to a DI-safe Double Burn blockstring, but loses to wakeup Drive Impact; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

cviper.name: Viper Cannon
cviper.notes: See Drive Impact. Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

cviper.name: Counter Spark (Block)
cviper.notes: Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; see Drive Reversal.

cviper.name: Counter Spark (Recovery)
cviper.notes: Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze except for a 12f freeze when interacting with the opponent's throw hitbox (this also refunds 1 Drive bar after punishing the throw); see Drive Reversal.

cviper.name: Drive Parry
cviper.notes: See Drive Parry. Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

cviper.name: Parry Drive Rush
cviper.notes: See Drive Rush; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.374 (min/throw), 1.756 (min/block), 3.355 (max/final DR frame)

cviper.name: Drive Rush Cancel
cviper.notes: See Drive Rush; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

cviper.name: High Jump
cviper.notes: Costs 1 bar of Drive gauge (except during SA1 install); jumps slightly higher and over 50% farther than a standard jump; can be input in neutral or canceled on hit/block from all normals (except 2HK/6MP/6HK) and from Seismic Hammer; can be input as a forward or neutral jump (cannot High Jump backwards, but attempting this as a cancel results in neutral jump); cancelable into grounded special moves and Supers during prejump frames 2-6, effectively allowing any HJ-cancelable attack to be special/super cancelable; C. Viper is in a Counter-hit state for the entire duration and in a Forced Knockdown state when airborne; Drive Gauge recovery acts similar to OD specials (can start regaining meter quickly, effectively refunding part of its cost by hitting the opponent afterward; grounded High Jump Cancel into grounded Burning Kick cannot be buffered on the first jump frame (results in a strict 2f window to properly input a combo sequence like juggled 5HK > HJC OD Burning Kick); can be used in safe jump setups with a KD Advantage of +45; the Up direction must be input no later than the 8th frame after initiating the Down direction (holding down before inputting a jump does not result in a High Jump); when canceled from a normal that is otherwise not special cancelable, execution requirements are relaxed and a neutral input is no longer required before the HJC (most useful for 2MK/2LK)

cviper.name: LP Thunder Dash
cviper.notes: Crouch-sized hurtbox on frames 14-43 (standing state); can be spaced meaty for better advantage (very precise spacing required for the final active frame to connect); can duck under projectiles with precise timing (impractical as a reaction to fast fireballs, and can be clipped on her back during recovery against slow fireballs); combos naturally from medium/heavy normals; punishing a projectile can link into 2MP, SA2, 5MK, or 2HP depending on the range; startup can be canceled into Feint by inputting K (feint occurs after 12 startup frames); cancelable into Tracer Combination (6PP) on hit/block only

cviper.name: MP Thunder Dash
cviper.notes: Less range than LP version but safe on block at all ranges; can be spaced meaty for better advantage; combos from 5LK naturally; startup can be canceled into Feint by inputting K (feint occurs after 8 startup frames); cancelable into Tracer Combination (6PP) on hit/block only; can perform a risky frame trap into follow-up on block (2f gap) unless the move connects on the final 2 active frames

cviper.name: HP Thunder Dash
cviper.notes: Upward trajectory for juggles and anti-airs; cannot hit cross-up; combos from all light normals; can whiff in long-range cancels like 5MK > HJC 214HP; startup can be canceled into Feint by inputting K (feint occurs after 6 startup frames, leading to the best advantage of all feint cancels); feint-canceled version still maintains anti-air invincibility on frames 1-6, allowing C.Viper to "spot dodge" some airborne attacks with precise timing for a better punish; variable knockdown advantage on airborne opponents; cancelable into Tracer Combination (6PP) on hit only (can whiff on high juggled opponents)

cviper.name: OD Thunder Dash
cviper.notes: 2 hits with a large gap in between; range of the 1st hit is in between LP/MP versions (total range is longer but easily interruptible if 1st hit whiffs); combos from medium and heavy normals; allows an easy hitconfirm into SA2/SA3 while remaining safe on block; leaves C.Viper inside throw range with block advantage on burned out opponents, making it a strong chip and pressure tool; cannot perform feint cancels or Tracer Combination follow-ups; if Perfect Parried, opponent can interrupt 2nd hit with 18f or faster attack; extremely disjointed hitbox makes it a strong approach tool at midrange; sets up a safe jump on grounded hit (midscreen, can only connect with max range j.MK)

cviper.name: Thunder Dash Feint
cviper.notes: Feint animation lasts 12f but occurs at a different timing from each meterless strength of Thunder Dash (LP 12+12 / MP 8+12 / HP 6+12); can be input more easily by holding any K while inputting 214P; 214HP version gives better combo potential from 2HP or from High Jump canceled 5HP/5HK; Counter-hit state for entire feint animation

cviper.name: LP Tracer Combination
cviper.notes: Costs 1 extra bar of Drive gauge (except during SA1 install); maintains the Projectile Invuln and crouch-sized hurtbox of 214LP on frames 1-17; best version for confirming into SA3 (combos naturally); forms a true blockstring from 214LP; gives solid oki with Drive Rush or a Forward Dash + manually timed walk

cviper.name: MP Tracer Combination
cviper.notes: Costs 1 extra bar of Drive gauge (except during SA1 install); cancel into SA3 does not combo on grounded opponents; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle OTG bounce state (KD +30 at lowest height, allows SA3 cancel to juggle); 2f gap on block can set up a risky frame trap (no gap during Burnout or if the final 2 active frames of 214MP connect); grounded hit gives the worst oki of all Thunder Dash follow-ups (-3 after Dash)

cviper.name: HP Tracer Combination
cviper.notes: Costs 1 extra bar of Drive gauge (except during SA1 install); can only be canceled into on hit; can whiff on high juggled opponents; gives the best oki out of all Thunder Dash follow-ups; useful way to extend C. Viper's anti-air damage

cviper.name: LK Burning Kick
cviper.notes: Shortest trajectory; cannot hit cross-up; Punish Counter gives an extra +5 KD advantage (allows combo into KK follow-up); primarily used for beating throw techs and crouching buttons; connects from about C. Viper's maximum poke range; very difficult to space more safely in neutral due to minimal forward movement during active frames

cviper.name: MK Burning Kick
cviper.notes: Medium trajectory; cannot hit cross-up; Punish Counter gives an extra +5 KD advantage (allows combo into KK follow-up); useful for crushing low pokes from outside their max range and for approaching in neutral while staying out of the opponent's throw range on block

cviper.name: HK Burning Kick
cviper.notes: Farthest trajectory; cannot hit cross-up; Punish Counter gives an extra +5 KD advantage (allows combo into KK follow-up); useful as a safe approach tool from long range (but more likely to land inside opponent's throw range on block); easiest version to space meaty for extra advantage due to forward movement during active frames; works well as a predictive fireball counter due to its range, safety, and lower body projectile invuln frames

cviper.name: OD Burning Kick
cviper.notes: Best horizontal range for combo consistency; 2 hits (cannot be interrupted on block); cannot hit cross-up; recovery is cancelable into SA2/SA3 after 11f on hit or block; very difficult to space meaty for extra advantage due to minimal forward movement during 2nd hit's active frames; important juggle tool after launches into Air Burning Kick or juggled 5HK ground bounce; combo from 5HK > HJC requires a strict 2f input window (cannot buffer on the first High Jump frame, and results in air version on frame 4 onward)

cviper.name: Knuckled Pursuit
cviper.notes: Costs 1 extra bar of Drive gauge (except during SA1 install); true blockstring and natural combo from Burning Kick; higher KD advantage if Burning Kick lands as a Punish Counter or hits airborne opponent; KD +9 when follow-up hits a grounded opponent (e.g. after Burning Kick is absorbed by 1-hit armor like Luke 236KK or Zangief Charged 5HP)

cviper.name: Double Burn
cviper.notes: Costs 1 extra bar of Drive gauge (except during SA1 install); leaves a 3f gap on block from Burning Kick that can beat non-invincible attacks (but loses to Drive Impact and anti-air invuln moves); true blockstring vs. opponents in Burnout and +6 oB making it a great pressure tool; KD +40 on grounded opponents (e.g. frame trap after Burning Kick) and +34 on airborne opponents (e.g. combo after PC Burning Kick or in juggle routes, up to KD +40 in very high juggles); does not combo naturally from Burning Kick on grounded opponents (requires Punish Counter or airborne connect); whiffing this attack on grounded hit results in a +13 knockdown with oki only possible in the corner

cviper.name: LK Aerial Burning Kick
cviper.notes: Can be input from a forward/neutral jump or High Jump; stops forward air momentum; can hit crossup; 1f extra landing recovery frame when blocked as a cross-up; 8f extra landing recovery on whiff after crossing over the opponent; comes out after 7 airborne frames (normal jump) or 3 airborne frames (High Jump); High Jump version deals 1f less blockstun but hits lower to the ground resulting in better advantage when used low to the ground; advantage on knockdown or block varies greatly depending on angle, distance, and height when activated; earliest input timing (Tiger Knee input) at close range results in KD +39 / -2 oB (regular jump), KD +43 / +1 oB (High Jump)

cviper.name: MK Aerial Burning Kick
cviper.notes: Can be input from a forward/neutral jump or High Jump; maintains some forward air momentum; can hit crossup; 1f extra landing recovery frame when blocked as a cross-up; 8f extra landing recovery on whiff after crossing over the opponent; comes out after 7 airborne frames (normal jump) or 3 airborne frames (High Jump); High Jump version deals 1f less blockstun but hits lower to the ground resulting in better advantage when used low to the ground; advantage on knockdown or block varies greatly depending on angle, distance, and height when activated; earliest input timing (Tiger Knee input) at close range results in KD +40 / -1 oB (regular jump), KD +43 / +1 oB (High Jump); using this version after Seismic Hammer launch allows a midscreen juggle into MP Thunder Dash + Tracer Combination (great damage, oki, and potential SA3 cancel with less meter cost than OD Burning Kick routes)

cviper.name: HK Aerial Burning Kick
